exercises.title: Sliding Heel Flexion with Strap
exercises.instructions: Sit comfortably on a firm bed or mat. Place a smooth towel or slider under your heel. Gently bend your knee, pulling your heel toward your buttocks using your leg muscles and a light tug with the strap. Hold at point of firm stretch without sharp pain.
exercises.precautions: Do not bounce. Keep your patella pointing toward the ceiling without turning your hip outwards.
exercises.doctorPrescriptionNote: PMR Dr. Dharshan: Crucial for breaking post-TKR arthrofibrosis before Week 4.

exercises.title: Terminal Knee Extension (TKE) with Resistance Band
exercises.instructions: Loop a green resistance band behind your operated knee with the other end secured to a heavy door anchor or bedpost. Stand facing the anchor. Start with your knee slightly bent, then straighten your knee fully against the band resistance, squeezing your quad tightly.
exercises.precautions: Keep your back straight. Do not hyperextend beyond neutral.
exercises.doctorPrescriptionNote: PMR Dr. Dharshan: Progressed from yellow band to green on Day 16.

exercises.title: Single Leg Weight Shifting & Proprioception
exercises.instructions: Stand upright with hands resting lightly on the kitchen counter for safety. Shift 80% of your body weight onto the operated right leg, feeling the floor through your whole foot. Maintain steady pelvic alignment.
exercises.precautions: Have a family member or sturdy support nearby at all times.
exercises.doctorPrescriptionNote: PMR Dr. Dharshan: Essential for preparing patient to discard stick safely.

exercises.title: Prone Quadriceps & Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.instructions: Lie flat on your stomach. If comfortable, loop a soft belt around your right ankle and gently pull your heel towards your glutes until a mild to moderate stretch is felt in the front of your thigh.
exercises.precautions: Stop if you feel anterior knee pinching or pain over the prosthesis.
exercises.doctorPrescriptionNote: PMR Dr. Dharshan: Keep pelvis flat on the bed to isolate the quadriceps.

blogs.title: Why PMR Doctor Monitoring Transforms Home Physiotherapy: Beyond Random Exercise
blogs.summary: Explore why having a medical specialist in Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation oversee every home physiotherapy session eliminates recovery plateaus and prevents dangerous post-op complications.
blogs.content:
### The Gap in Modern Home Rehabilitation

When a patient undergoes major surgery or suffers a neurological event like a stroke, the hospital stay is often brief. Within days, they are back home in their living room. In traditional home care models, a freelance physiotherapist is contracted to visit 3 to 5 times a week.

While physical therapists possess wonderful hands-on techniques, a critical clinical gap exists: **the absence of continuous medical supervision**.

A physiatrist (PMR Doctor - Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation) is an MD physician specifically trained to evaluate musculoskeletal, neurological, and cardiopulmonary systems as an integrated functional unit. 

### What Happens When a PMR Doctor Tracks Every Session?

1. **Early Detection of Surgical Complications**:
After joint replacements or spinal microdiscectomies, subtle warning signs—such as asymmetric calf edema (early DVT), incision stitch abscess, or localized heat—are often missed by patients. Our PMR doctors evaluate the session vitals and therapist photographs after every single visit.

2. **Dynamic Protocol Titration**:
Healing is not linear. One day a patient has an effusion flare-up; the next day their neuromuscular recruitment accelerates. Rather than waiting for a 6-week surgeon appointment, the PMR physician recalibrates the load, range of motion targets, and resistance bands in real time.

3. **Objective Biomarkers & Outcome Tracking**:
Every session captures digital goniometer angles, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain levels, and timed functional scores. This data feeds into a medical-grade recovery model that predicts discharge milestones.

4. **Seamless Medical Collaboration**:
If a patient requires a pharmacological adjustment—such as neuropathic pain medication or anti-spasticity agents—the PMR doctor liaises directly with the treating surgeon or neurologist.

### The Result: 40% Shorter Time to Full Independence

Clinical trials in rehabilitation medicine demonstrate that physician-supervised tele-rehabilitation combined with certified home therapists produces statistically superior functional independence measures (FIM) and significantly lower readmission rates compared to unguided home care.

blogs.title: Total Knee Replacement: Why 115-Degree Flexion Depends on Doctor-Monitored Home Sessions
blogs.summary: The first 30 days post-TKR determine your lifelong mobility. Learn the physiological stages of scar tissue and how PMR physician guidance prevents knee arthrofibrosis.
blogs.content:
### The 30-Day Race Against Arthrofibrosis

Following total knee arthroplasty, the body initiates a robust inflammatory cascade. Collagen fibers begin cross-linking to heal surgical incisions and capsular tissue. If physical therapy is too gentle, the joint capsule contracts, permanently locking the knee at 70° to 80° flexion. If therapy is too aggressive, joint effusion triggers arthrogenic muscle inhibition, shutting down the quadriceps.

This delicate biological tightrope is why **PMR doctor monitoring is game-changing**.

### The Clinical Milestones We Track at Home

- **Week 1 (Days 1–7)**: Passive knee extension to 0°. Eliminating extensor lag is critical; walking with a flexed knee overloads the opposite hip and lumbar spine.
- **Week 2 (Days 8–14)**: Active flexion crossing 90°. This allows comfortable sitting on standard dining chairs and using commodes independently.
- **Week 3 (Days 15–21)**: Active flexion 105° to 110°. Stair ascent initiation with reciprocal stepping.
- **Week 4–6**: Active flexion 115° to 125°. Normal gait velocity without assistive walking devices.

### How PhysioPMR Clinicians Address Pain Spikes

When a patient experiences a pain spike from VAS 3 to VAS 7, conventional therapy might halt exercises altogether or push through dangerous inflammation. In our model:
1. The therapist logs the exact joint circumference and pain rating.
2. The PMR physician reviews the log within hours and differentiates between capsular stretch pain vs pes anserine bursitis or patellofemoral friction.
3. The exercise prescription is modified on the spot with targeted closed-chain modifications and cryo-compression protocols.

blogs.title: Stroke Rehabilitation at Home: Neuroplasticity, Spasticity & The Physiatrist's Touch
blogs.summary: Neuroplasticity is at its zenith during the first 3 months post-stroke. How our PMR-led home neurological rehab protocol reprograms motor pathways safely.
blogs.content:
### Harnessing the Neuroplastic Window

Following an ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, undamaged areas of the cerebral cortex can adapt to assume functions previously governed by damaged neural tissue. This biological miracle is known as **neuroplasticity**.

However, neuroplasticity is a double-edged sword: if a patient practices abnormal compensatory patterns (e.g. severe hip hiking, abnormal circumduction gait, or internal shoulder rotation synergy), the brain hardwires those pathological motor schemas.

### The PMR Doctor's Neurological Assessment Protocol

In our home neurological program, our physiatrist tracks:
- **Brunnstrom Stages of Motor Recovery**
- **Modified Ashworth Scale for Muscle Spasticity**
- **Berg Balance Scale for Fall Risk Assessment**
- **Functional Independence Measure (FIM) for Activities of Daily Living**

When spasticity in the calf or bicep threatens to cause fixed contractures, the PMR physician initiates serial antispasticity positioning, electrical stimulation protocols, and coordinates with the patient's neurologist for oral or focal treatments.

Home-based therapy allows training in the patient's actual living environment—their real bathroom thresholds, bedside transfers, and kitchen counters—accelerating practical autonomy.

blogs.title: Preventing Senior Falls at Home: Why Walking Alone Isn't Enough
blogs.summary: 1 in 3 adults over 65 falls annually. Discover how targeted vestibular exercises, gluteal strengthening, and PMR home environmental audits safeguard elderly loved ones.
blogs.content:
### Walking Is Great, But It Does Not Train Reactive Balance

Many elderly individuals and their families believe that a morning walk in the garden is sufficient to maintain mobility. While cardiovascular walking is beneficial, it fails to train three critical fall-prevention mechanisms:
1. **Proprioceptive Joint Sense**: The neurological ability of ankle receptors to detect uneven ground surfaces.
2. **Vestibular-Ocular Reflex (VOR)**: Stabilizing visual focus on a target while the head is moving.
3. **Reactive Stepping Velocity**: The rapid forward or lateral step triggered automatically when stumbling over a rug or pet.

Our physiatrist-led geriatric fall prevention program combines dual-task cognitive-motor drills with dynamic balance challenges in the safety of home.

blogs.title: Sciatica & Lumbar Disc Herniation: What to Do in the First 14 Days at Home
blogs.summary: Acute back spasms and radiating leg pain require precise directional preference therapy. How McKenzie principles and PMR monitoring avoid unnecessary spine surgery.
blogs.content:
### Centralization vs Peripheralization: The Golden Clinical Rule

When a lumbar intervertebral disc bulges and impinges on the L4, L5, or S1 nerve root, pain travels down the posterior leg—a condition known as sciatica.

In our home rehabilitation protocol, the PMR physician instructs therapists to constantly monitor **the direction of symptom migration**:
- **Centralization**: Pain moves out of the foot and calf up into the low back. This is an objective sign that mechanical pressure on the nerve root is diminishing.
- **Peripheralization**: Pain shoots further down toward the toes or accompanies motor weakness (foot drop). This requires immediate clinical repositioning and medical escalation.

With guided home extension positioning and gentle neurodynamic nerve flossing, over 85% of disc herniations resolve conservatively without surgery.
